name: Tebaliah
overview: Tebaliah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, known specifically as the third-born son of Hosah. His identity is grounded in this familial and tribal connection as recorded in 1 Chronicles 26:11. There are no additional notes on his life or role beyond this genealogical detail.
namesAndTitles: The name Tebaliah means 'YHWH has dipped,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's involvement or blessing. This proper name, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 26:11, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries significant meaning within the Hebrew context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Tebaliah as the son of Hosah. Beyond this, there are no further family relationships detailed in the biblical text concerning Tebaliah.
scriptureSignificance: Tebaliah’s significance in Scripture lies primarily in his place within the Levitical genealogy, marking him as part of the priestly tribe dedicated to service in the temple. His identification as the third-born son of Hosah situates him within the historical record of Levitical families, which were crucial for maintaining the spiritual and liturgical functions ordained by God. While no further narrative details are given, his mention preserves the continuity of God’s chosen lineage among the Levites.
